what: The replay of a third party's Lean proof that joins the two claimed refutations of the Exponential Time Hypothesis: TSavo's Bridge.ethIsFalse_of_claim : OAI.Algorithms.SubexponentialSAT.SqrtLogSpace.Claim → MainResults.ETHIsFalse (github.com/TSavo/eth-bridge @ 34f9ca20; OpenAI's challenge statement as a proposition implies Anthropic's ETHIsFalse), built inside Anthropic's eth project at 16a5ce41 as its README says, decided by tools/record-eth-tsavo.js from a GitHub-hosted run of .github/workflows/eth-tsavo.yml. CERTIFIED here means the statements are the two labs' own (checked byte for byte against our pins), the theorem states exactly Claim → ETHIsFalse, uses only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, and two independently written kernels accept it. It does NOT mean that ETH is false: the implication needs OpenAI's Claim, which OpenAI proved (certs/eth-kernel.json) on another Lean and Mathlib (see gaps), and no machine checks that MainResults.ETH is the textbook hypothesis (corpus/eth-refutation/readings/).
campaign: eth-refutation; the TSavo bridge lane (the claim was posted on anthropics/formal-math#36 with a request for a check); pins recorded before any run (corpus/eth-refutation/tsavo/pins.json)

words.CERTIFIED: the statement checks pass on the run's bytes; Comparator exit 0 with "Your solution is okay!"; Lean's kernel and nanoda both accept; lake build Bridge exit 0; #print axioms (our file) names only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound for both theorems

words.REFUSED: no decision, with the exact reason (resources, a build failure, bytes differing from the pins, a statement check, Comparator stopping on its own check, kernels disagreeing, or one kernel rejection not yet reproduced)

why: the statement checks pass on the run's bytes; Comparator exit 0 with "Your solution is okay!" on TSavo's config (with the declared lakefile amendment); Lean's kernel and nanoda both accept; lake build Bridge exit 0; both theorems' axioms are among propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
gaps: TSavo's README build does not run Comparator on TSavo's own config: on the README's lakefile (Anthropic's, plus [[lean_lib]] Bridge, srcDir "bridge", globs ["Bridge.+"]) Comparator stops at "Building BridgeChallenge" because Lake reports unknown target `BridgeChallenge` (exit 1): the glob Bridge.+ names Bridge and its submodules, and BridgeChallenge is neither. The replay declares ONE amendment, a [[lean_lib]] named BridgeChallenge with srcDir "bridge" appended to the lakefile (no Lean byte and no config byte changes), and decides on the run with it. TSavo's README says Anthropic's CI script accepted the bridge on 2026-10-27; the lakefile that run used must have made BridgeChallenge resolvable, and the README does not show how.

The seam between the two lanes is the Lean and Mathlib version: the bridge's Claim is OpenAI's challenge text re-elaborated on Lean v4.33.1 and Anthropic's Mathlib 0df444a3, while OpenAI's proof (certs/eth-kernel.json) is of exact_count_and_sat on Lean v4.34.1 and Mathlib d13f23b7. The source text is the same byte for byte (the statement check); that the two elaborate to the same term is not checked here, so OpenAI's theorem and TSavo's implication compose by reading, not by one kernel.

Comparator decides Bridge.ethIsFalse_of_claim only (the config's one theorem). Bridge.two_proofs_one_statement = ⟨MainResults.ethIsFalse, ethIsFalse_of_claim⟩ is checked by one kernel (Lean's, in lake build) and by its axiom print.
A stale comment: bridge/Bridge/Main.lean's header still says "Each `sorry` below is one of the four lemmas named in the plan"; no sorry remains outside comments (the census).
leanchecker --fresh was not run on this join (the eth-kernel lane replayed both claims' own proofs with it, not the join); the rule stands on Lean's kernel and nanoda inside Comparator.
closes: What the theorem moves out of prose, if CERTIFIED: our reading of OpenAI's claim (corpus/eth-refutation/readings/first.md §I.4) needs B1 (a PrimitiveMachine simulated with polynomial overhead) and B2 (a plain 3-CNF rewritten into encodeCNF in polynomial time), both by eye. TSavo proves, in Lean, B1 into Anthropic's model (a PrimitiveMachine as a Groundwork.Stepped computation, compiled to a Mathlib FinTM2 machine by Anthropic's exists_tm, its state size bounded by OpenAI's own visited-space bound) and B2 from Anthropic's plain 3-CNF code (a polynomial-time map from Sat3.enc to encodeCNF, insertion sort proved equal to Finset.sort), then Anthropic's own lemma WidthThree.ethFails_of_subexpTM carries Sat3.SubexpTM to MainResults.ETHIsFalse, so OpenAI's Claim lands on Anthropic's ETHIsFalse. What stays prose is then Anthropic's own step from FinTM2 on encClauses to the textbook hypothesis (B1′, B2′ of the same reading), the step certs/eth-bridge.json also leaves to prose. Only ClaimAt 3 is used.

openaiStatement.reads: Claim = ∀ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → ClaimAt k, ClaimAt k = the 23 statement lines of exact_count_and_sat; the 23 lines never name hk, so ∀ (k) (hk : 2 ≤ k), S k and ∀ k, 2 ≤ k → ClaimAt k are the same proposition up to unfolding ClaimAt
openaiStatement.change: theorem exact_count_and_sat (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) : <23 lines> := by sorry  →  def ClaimAt (k : ℕ) : Prop := <the same 23 lines>, plus def Claim : Prop := ∀ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → ClaimAt k; undoing it gives the pinned bytes
